summary: Ground-mounted L-4 cab on Coldwater Peak from 1935 to 1968; the cabin is gone and the summit now holds research instruments, reached by a hiking trail.

facts.status_note: The cabin was removed in 1968; the summit now holds research instruments, not a lookout.

staffing.as_of: 1937 (last staffing item found in sources read)

access.note: Summit reached by a hiking trail in Mount St. Helens National Volcanic Monument; the winter road is gated at Coldwater Lake and the trail starts about a mile past the gate.

visit.trail_note: Hike from the Johnson Visitors Center area. The cabin was removed, so there is no lookout to climb.

events.note: Developed as a ground-mounted L-4 cab; Wikipedia gives the lookout years as 1935 to 1968
A July 1937 item says the Cold Water Peak lookout position was being filled by an experienced man
A May 1964 item says three Spirit Lake district lookouts, one named Coldwater Creek, would close that summer except for possible emergency use; the item does not explicitly name this cabin
Registered June 23, 2012 as US 1310, WA 210; nominated by Ray Kresek

evidence.supports: lookout 1935 to 1968; now a site for research instruments; reached by a trail
evidence.quote: A trail provides access to the summit, the site of the former Coldwater Lookout from 1935 to 1968, and now is a site for research instruments.

evidence.supports: summit located in Mount St. Helens National Volcanic Monument
evidence.quote: Coldwater Peak is a 5,722 ft (1,740 m) mountain summit located in Mount St. Helens National Volcanic Monument

evidence.supports: built 1935 as a ground-mounted L-4 cab; one of the choicest views of Mount St. Helens
evidence.quote: Developed in 1935, this ground-mounted L-4 cab certainly had one of the choicest views of Mt. St. Helens.

evidence.supports: built around 1935 as a ground-mounted L-4 cab
evidence.quote: The old fire lookout was built around 1935. It was a ground-mounted L-4 cab.

evidence.supports: July 1937 item: position filled by an experienced man
evidence.quote: In 1937 the Cold Water Peak Lookout position on the Columbia Forest is being filled by an experienced man.

evidence.supports: May 1964 Longview Daily News item: Spirit Lake district lookouts to close, one named Coldwater Creek
evidence.quote: The three lookouts in the Spirit Lake ranger district -- at Vanson Peak, Strawberry Mountain and Coldwater Creek -- will be closed this summer, except for possible emergency use.

evidence.supports: cabin removed in 1968; the 1980 eruption would have destroyed it had it survived
evidence.quote: The cabin was removed in 1968, but had it survived to 1980, the eruption of St. Helens would have obliterated the lookout.

evidence.supports: lookout years 1935 to 1968; cabin removed in 1968
hiking access from the Johnson Visitors Center
evidence.quote: Hiking from the Johnson Visitors Center, Coldwater is the first mountain of real prominence.

evidence.supports: site used for research instruments today
evidence.quote: Once a sight of a lookout tower, today it is the site for numerous research instruments.

evidence.supports: winter road up to Johnson Ridge Visitors Center gated at Coldwater Lake
evidence.quote: During the winter, the road up to Johnson Ridge Visitors Center is closed, gated at Coldwater Lake.

evidence.supports: trail starts about a mile past the winter gate
evidence.quote: But, the Coldwater Trail starts about a mile past the gate so the mountain can be reached during this time period.

notes_for_editor: Built date 1935 agrees across the register, Willhite and Wikipedia; removal in 1968 agrees across the register, FireLookout.com and Wikipedia. The 1964 closure notice names Coldwater Creek, not Coldwater Peak, and the page files it under this lookout without saying they are the same; the story flags that. The record's access is unknown; sources describe a public hiking route, so access is set to public. Staffing rests on one 1937 item. No source describes footings or other remains on the summit today. Summit elevation (5,722 ft, Wikipedia) and lookout-site elevation (5,727 ft, register) differ slightly; both are measurements of nearby points.
